bypass_fail_closed.assertion: The bypass SLOT remained durably present in main but replay closed the block with score=1 for that slot.

mixed_legacy_history.assertion: A legacy closed row replayed unchanged, followed by a compliance row whose bypass slot was forced to 1; reporter state advanced from the two scientific rows.

measurement_validity_rules: Scientific closure is defined by the rederived reservation-compliance row, not historical atomic SLOT acceptance.
A bound SLOT lacking only COMMIT must be reconciled before CLOSE so crash bookkeeping cannot silently discard a valid durable score; unreconciled attempts cannot be closed as compliant.
The compliance audit payload and its digest are embedded in CLOSE and rederived from the exact pre-CLOSE main prefix plus reservation ledger on replay.
A torn compliance CLOSE never partially advances reporting state; only the complete checksummed CLOSE commits the scientific row.
Legacy closed rows are replayable without reinterpretation; the new rule applies to compliance CLOSE events.
deployment_blocker: The old durable_k_guard_hybrid_journal replay and old launch-capability gate still bind the legacy reporting adapter. After a compliance CLOSE whose audited row differs from legacy SLOT acceptance, those old components will reject/reconstruct the wrong state. A new gate/runtime replay binding must be installed before deploying compliance CLOSE.
next_action: Create a compliance-aware launch-capability gate/runtime adapter that uses reservation_compliance_close_replay for all post-close recovery while preserving legacy ADMIT acknowledgement, then byte-execute the full ADMIT -> RESERVE -> SCORE -> bound SLOT -> COMMIT -> compliance CLOSE -> next ADMIT lifecycle against repository-local sibling files.
